subject: Preflight: concurrency bucketing, burst windows & token latency probe
messages:
From: Priyanka Sharma <priyanka@starlift.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing: preliminary traffic snapshot & a few clarifications

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking this — we kicked off a dedicated-fleet evaluation internally and put together a quick snapshot (attached) but wanted to clarify a few items before we fill out any long forms: 

- Expected steady-state concurrency: 180 sessions, but we expect short bursts up to ~1,400 concurrent sessions during product launches (bursts last 3–8 minutes).
- Prompt/response sizes: median prompt ~120 tokens, 95th-response ~1,400 tokens (some responses are long-form summaries).
- We rely on session KV caching (customer conversation histories) for stateful assistant features; cache hit rate today ~62%.
- Hard constraints: GDPR data residency in EU for some customer segments, but primary workload is US-based.

Can you share your pre-sales intake that captures burst windows, bucketed concurrency, and token-latency expectations? Also curious what conservative GPU SKUs you’d recommend for a pilot (4–8 week canary).

Attaching our CSV snapshot for Q2 traffic.

Best,
Priyanka
Priyanka Sharma
Head of Platform Ops, Starlift

Attachment: starlift-traffic-2025Q2.csv (CSV, 54KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Priyanka Sharma <priyanka@starlift.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing: preliminary traffic snapshot & a few clarifications

Hi Priyanka — thanks for the snapshot, that helps a lot. Looping Marissa (sales) and Karthik (inference sizing) to help with SKU and pilot design.

Below is a short intake we use to convert CSV snapshots into a dedicated sizing hypothesis — answers to these will speed us up: 

1) Peak burst profile: when you say 1,400 concurrent sessions, is that a single contiguous 3–8 minute burst or multiple overlapping bursts across regions?
2) Bot session semantics: are sessions long-lived (5–30 minutes) with many short messages, or short-lived single-query sessions? Approx session duration and avg messages per session.
3) Response tail: you listed 95th-response at ~1,400 tokens. Are those outliers tied to a specific flow (exports, reports) or general chat responses?
4) KV cache behavior: please confirm avg KV per-session (kb) and whether KV can be truncated for pilot traffic.
5) SLOs: target P95 token-response latency (ms) and acceptable P99 (ms) under burst.
6) Security/compliance: any additional requirements beyond GDPR (e.g., customer-managed keys, SOC reports)?

I attached our compact intake template (redwood-dedicated-intake-template.csv) — fill the highlighted fields and we’ll produce a first-pass GPU mix and occupancy model. Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow to review answers and pick SKUs? Proposed times: 11:00AM or 3:00PM PT.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Pre-Sales — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-intake-template.csv (CSV, 8KB)

Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing: preliminary traffic snapshot & a few clarifications

Lauren — quick answers inline and attaching our SOW draft so you can see timeline constraints: 

1) Burst shape: single contiguous burst for launches (3–8 minutes) that hits most of our serving pool; occasional overlapping smaller bursts across regions but primary risk is the single launch window.
2) Sessions: mostly medium-lived sessions (8–22 minutes), avg ~6 messages per session. Some automated flows (report generation) are long-running.
3) Response tail: 95th tied to an "export+summarize" flow and a few customer-facing long reads — not every user.
4) KV: avg per-session KV ~45KB (conversation + metadata). We can truncate history to 3 messages for pilot if needed (reduce KV to ~10–12KB).
5) SLOs: target P95 token latency ~120ms, acceptable P99 ~450ms during burst.
6) Security: must support EU residency for a subset; prefer to evaluate with Redwood Private later, but pilot can run in Redwood Dedicated US region. We will need SOC 2 report and an initial security questionnaire completed.

Attached: starlift-sow-v0.1.docx (SOW, 92KB)

We can do tomorrow 11:00AM PT — please send invite.

Thanks — Priyanka

Attachment: starlift-sow-v0.1.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Priyanka Sharma <priyanka@starlift.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 Aug 2025 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing: preliminary traffic snapshot & a few clarifications

Thanks for the quick answers, Priyanka — that helps us narrow recommendations. A few follow-ups and an early SKU suggestion from Karthik: 

- Pilot goal & staging: 4–6 week pilot with a canary serving ~25% of launch traffic, then scale to full pilot. That lets us validate burst behaviour without over-committing.
- SKU suggestion (conservative): A mix of A100-80GB (for long-response/high-kv flows) plus a small pool of H200 (or equivalent) for high-throughput short responses. Karthik, can you add a quick occupancy calc?
- KV cache: truncating history to 3 messages will materially reduce GPU memory pressure — please confirm if you can accept slightly degraded conversational continuity during pilot.
- SLO reconciliation: hitting P95 ~120ms during launch will be tight if all traffic hits long-read flows. Recommendation: for the pilot, set a P95 target of 160ms and measure impact; if we see headroom, tighten to 120ms for final SLA.

Karthik — sending you the intake + CSV; can you return a conservative occupancy model (tokens/sec per-GPU, expected concurrent sessions per-GPU) before our 11AM slot so we can present numbers in the call?

Lauren — I’ll draft an agenda and send calendar invite for 11:00AM PT.

— Marissa
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
